title: Neisseria meningitidis: Biology, Microbiology, and Epidemiology (Rouphael & Stephens)

claims.text: Neisseria meningitidis (the meningococcus) remains a leading cause worldwide of bacterial meningitis.
claims.byte_quote: the meningococcus remains a leading cause worldwide of bacterial meningitis

claims.text: Overall mortality in invasive meningococcal disease today is 10-15% (was 70-85% fatal in the pre-antibiotic era).
claims.byte_quote: In the pre-serum therapy and pre-antibiotic eras, 70–85% of meningococcal disease cases were fatal; today, the overall mortality rate in invasive meningococcal disease still remains high, at between 10 and 15%

claims.text: There are an estimated 1.2 million cases of meningococcal infection per year worldwide, with ~135,000 deaths.
claims.byte_quote: There are an estimated 1.2 million cases of meningococcal infection per year, with a death toll of ~135,000 worldwide

claims.text: In the USA the meningococcal attack rate is now less than one case per 100,000 per year.
claims.byte_quote: In the USA, the attack rate is now less than one case per 100,000 per year

claims.text: Infants under 1 year have the highest incidence of meningococcal disease, 5.38 cases per 100,000.
claims.byte_quote: Infants aged <1 year have the highest incidence of meningococcal disease (5.38 cases per 100,000)

claims.text: The meningococcus is a common cause of bacterial meningitis in children and young adults in the USA, now mostly affecting children less than 2 years of age.
claims.byte_quote: a common cause of bacterial meningitis in children and young adults in the USA ( 132 ), now mostly affecting children less than 2 years of age

claims.text: Two-thirds of US meningococcal disease in the first year of life occurs in infants under 6 months of age.
claims.byte_quote: Two-thirds of meningococcal disease in the first year of life in the US occurs in infants less than 6 months of age

claims.text: N. meningitidis is a fastidious, encapsulated, aerobic gram-negative diplococcus.
claims.byte_quote: N. meningitidis is a fastidious, encapsulated, aerobic gram-negative diplococcus

claims.text: N. meningitidis is an encapsulated or unencapsulated aerobic diplococcus with a 'kidney' or 'coffee-bean' shape.
claims.byte_quote: is either an encapsulated or unencapsulated, aerobic diplococcus with a “kidney” or “coffee-bean” shape

claims.text: On CSF Gram stain, meningococcal meningitis shows intracellular gram-negative diplococci and leukocytes.
claims.byte_quote: Intracellular gram-negative diplococci and leukocytes in the CSF from a patient with meningococcal meningitis
